Patch Set 10: Code-Review+2
Change has been successfully merged
Since you're still within this namespace, I don't think you need to specify it?

There are SensorDefinition struct definitions in both the parent (`phosphor::fan::monitor`) and child (`phosphor::fan::monitor::multi_chassis`) namespaces, so this is to specify that a SensorDefinition from the parent namespace is being used.
This can be wrapped in an std::move() to avoid a copy.
Done.
could you move this to the top?  That's where constructors usually are.
Done, moved to top.
mem_fn isn't needed anymore.  You can just use std::bind or bind_front.
I removed this instance altogether, since we're passing in the powerState object, but I changed another case of mem_fn in the same file.

Added this getter function to the Fan class and extracted the Fan constructor code into an init() function to avoid DBus call errors. Wrote a test case to check that the proper number of fans were created.
Power state would be a property of the parent chassis.  So for now you could just pass it in like the thermal alert.
Changed it to a passed in reference like the thermalAlert.
Can we just leave all of the protected functions out of this class?
Removed them.
I think you need to add zone_test.cpp in here

If you run local CI, at the end it will have a line like "Full test results in .../build/meson-logs/testlog.txt"

If you edit that file, you can see each test suite that is run and what test cases within it run. Then you can verify whether your new tests actually ran.
Added that and other dependencies required to get the tests to run and pass.
This is no longer needed? I didn't see it in the moved ctor at the top of the updated file.
As Matt mentioned above, _powerState is a property of the parent chassis not the zone, so I'm just passing in a reference versus instantiating in the constructor.

Good job getting this in there. It is easy to forget in an abstract base class, but without a virtual dtor declared here you will leak memory when child classes assigned to a ZoneBase& or ZoneBase* are destructed.
Thanks!
nit: can you add the @brief like the others have?
I added the @brief annotation to the variables in this file that I created. I can add it to more if needed.

I'm not sure, but I'm guessing test_sources was supposed to be a common list of source files used by one or more of the test cases.

If you end up creating more test executables, it might be less copy/paste to move the list above into test_sources.  Then use test_sources in the new executable too.

Another option is to build a static library with all the non-test .cpp files except the one containing main(). Then link that library into both the application and the test cases.

Neither of these needs to be done in this commit or ever. Just a suggestion.

Yeah, if there ends up being lots of source overlap between test executables, I can probably move some of the sources into the test_sources variable. There isn't a lot between the two I've made so far, so maybe not an immediate thing, but something to consider for the future.

other than the EXPECT calls, is there any other difference between the 2 testcases?

If not, they could be combined into one.  I'm not a big proponent of needing separate testcases to test every method call when it causes a lot of duplication.

In fact, the isPowerOn() is never really going to test interesting code anyway, so you could probably even just skip it since it's almost 100 lines of setup.

The only differences are the EXPECT calls and that the fan creation test calls the init() function for zones. Otherwise, they're the same. I'll remove the power on test for now since we can't power on from the unit tests anyway.

Instead of all Zone instances having to watch for the same thing, ideally I think whatever class you'll have just 1 of could watch this and filter down the calls.

Can be done in the future though.

It also might be possible that the inventory won't even be necessary anymore.
does the fan init() also have to run here?
Yeah, I think it should, since the config is being reloaded here.

Did this change break something for single-chassis systems?

Also, I realize the ifdefs are not needed since no JSON parsing is happening. But is there still a difference here between YAML-based and JSON-based operation?

So, the getJsonObj() call was causing errors with the unit tests since it tries to search a path for a json config to use to set the trust manager. Since trust groups are an older workaround that don't need to be supported anymore, I removed that call and had it create and store an empty trust manager instead (since you still need one to pass to the Fan constructor). As for whether there is a difference between yaml and json operation, Matt had said that the new fan monitor code doesn't need to support yaml, so I haven't made much differentiation. 

With that being said, might be able to remove the setTrustMgr() and/or getTrustGroups() functions from this file, since we're not doing much with the trust groups. I'll ask Matt about it after next week.
are all of these headers needed here?

I would think the top ones `(fan, fan_error, ...)` would be needed, since classes and functions from those are being used here or in `zone.cpp`. `<memory>`, `<optional>`, and `<vector>` are also used as are json and bus/event. I removed the source headers.
I don't think a lot of these headers are needed?
I removed most of them, but kept fan and tach_sensor and added set/map, since those are used here.

Based on suggestion from Matt, added test fixture class to share common setup code between test cases. Added a getter for the zone name to match Zone objects to ZoneDefinition structs in the upcoming Chassis class. Removed the power on test case and used a literal for chassis_nums vector rather than declaring a variable.
Removed getTrustGroups and setTrustMgr since trust groups are no longer supported. Removed getName for now since not required for Chassis class at the moment.
Moved some includes from zone.hpp to zone.cpp
